title: GradingBatch
description:
A read — the R-dev pilot, R-dev, R-conf, a pointed read: the unit that fixes the rubric, the readers, the per-reader order seed and the status of the read. The same record is returned to an admin and to a reader; it carries per-reader PROGRESS COUNTS and never a verdict. A batch the caller may not see — neither an admin nor one of its `readers` — is a 404, indistinguishable from an unknown id (ADR-0003 §2).

**Status.** `open`: readers save verdicts; nobody, including an admin, can read another reader's row. `adjudicating` (after POST …/adjudicate): reader rows are frozen (a PUT is 409), visible to admins only, and the joint-read verdict can be saved. `closed` is reserved by docs/plans/grading-ui.md §3.1 for a later phase — no v1 operation produces it, and nothing in v1 requires it (the export is available from `adjudicating` on).

**Reader order.** Each reader sees the batch's tasks in a private, deterministic permutation computed from (`order_seed`, the reader's position in `readers`): reader at index k (label A for 0, B for 1, …) sees the tasks in batch order permuted by CPython's `random.Random(order_seed + k + 1).shuffle(list(range(task_count)))` — the exact rule `docs/plans/results/stage0/s0_rdev.py` uses to build the `RDEV-readsheet-A/B.html` sheets (seed+1 for A, seed+2 for B), so a read begun on those sheets continues in the UI at the same position. The rule is normative for every implementation (MT19937 seeded with the integer; Python ≥ 3.2's `shuffle`), which is what makes two implementations show one reader one order.

id.description: Opaque server-assigned batch id (a uuid4 hex).

name.description: Human-readable name of the read (`R-dev pilot r3`, `R-dev`, …).

kind.description: The protocol every task of this batch follows; see `GradingTask.kind`.

rubric_sha256.description: sha256 (64 lowercase hex) of the frozen rubric the readers signed off on (SPEC §6.6.1: `design/RUBRIC-evidence.md`). Shown in the grading view; recorded so a verdict can never be attributed to a rubric other than the one it was read under.

order_seed.description: The integer seed the per-reader orders derive from (see the schema description). The study's `SEED_RDEV` for the R-dev read.

readers.description: Resolved subjects of the readers, in LABEL order: index 0 is reader `A`, 1 is `B`, … The label is what the export's CSV filenames carry (`rdev_verdicts_A.csv`) and what `s0_rdev_score.py --a/--b` means.

task_count.description: Number of tasks in the batch.

progress.description: One entry per reader in label order: how many of the batch's tasks that reader has saved a verdict on. Counts, never verdicts — this is what a reader sees of the other reader, and all of it.

created_by.description: Subject of the admin who created the batch. Recorded for audit; it confers nothing — every admin may administer every batch.

adjudicating_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the POST …/adjudicate that froze the readers' rows; empty string while `open` (the same empty-string-while-not-yet convention as `ShareRecord.revoked_at`).

label.description: The reader's letter label (`A`, `B`, …), by position in `readers`.

saved.description: Tasks on which this reader has a current verdict (0 ≤ saved ≤ task_count).
